jamal-reid: Heads up, after installing redwoodctl via snap on Ubuntu 22.04, `redwoodctl local test` ignores my `--profile` and also fails to pick up token rotation. Using snap 1.2.0 from edge channel. Anyone run into snap confinement weirdness with profile files?
lisa-chen: snaps run confined under strict interfaces. Where are your config files? Snap packages usually see $HOME as `/root` inside the snap unless classic is used.
jamal-reid: config I expected at ~/.config/redwood/config.json but `strace` shows the binary opening `/home/jamal/snap/redwoodctl/common/.redwood/config.json` first. The file there is stale (contains old token). I removed it but the command recreates it after login.
mohan: that's the snap state dir. We ship a snap that writes a default config into the snap state on first run which is problematic when users later migrate via XDG env var. We should stop seeding tokens into the snap state.
jamal-reid: issue also: when token rotates (OIDC refresh) the client calls `POST /auth/refresh` and gets 500 intermittently, our retry logic retries 2 times but backoff is linear and too short causing immediate auth failure in local test harness. I can reproduce with `RUST_LOG=debug redwoodctl auth refresh --debug`.
deploy-bot: Created issue devex/cli#4701 "snap-installed redwoodctl seeds stale state and short auth retry backoff" - https://github.com/redwood-inference/devex/issues/4701 :white_check_mark:
lisa-chen: quick workaround: install via official .deb or curl install script for now, or run `snap run --classic redwoodctl` if you installed classic snap. Also `rm -rf ~/snap/redwoodctl/common/.redwood && redwoodctl login --persist` will re-seed correctly.
mohan: opened PR with two fixes: 1) Avoid writing tokens into snap state on first-run (seed skeleton only), 2) bump auth refresh retry to exponential backoff with jitter (up to 5 tries) and surfaced a clearer error when all retries fail. PR: devex/cli#4703.
anya: nice. For local testing we should also add a `--no-state` flag for ephemeral runs (useful in CI) that ignores any on-disk config and reads token only from env or CLI. Could help reproducibility.
jamal-reid: +1 on `--no-state`. For now I hacked `REDWOOD_STATE_DIR=/tmp/nonexistent redwoodctl local test --profile ci` which worked.
devx-bot: Note: adding `--no-state` to roadmap item CLI-239. If anyone needs the CI hack, paste `REDWOOD_STATE_DIR=/tmp/ci_state redwoodctl local test --token $TOKEN` to avoid snap state.
mohan: Scheduled canary for PR on staging tomorrow. Will also add an integration test that exercises snap install path in CI matrix.
jamal-reid: confirmed workaround works and tests pass in my env. Thanks folks.
devx-bot: Closing thread when PR merges; please react with :thumbsup: if you want `--no-state` priority bumped.
